candidate.note: v0.6.0 release candidate: branch-aware memory tiers and a promotion ladder (#16/#18/#19/#21/#38), capsule size and convergence work with a terminal-state repair, new `memex jobs` / `recover` / `install` commands, doctor checks, honest injection logging, docs, and a `--both` search fix. All thirteen gates plus the full acceptance benchmark ran on this clean committed SHA; `git status --porcelain` was empty before them and HEAD was unchanged after, and `npm run build` reproduced the tracked dist/ byte-for-byte. Unlike v0.5.1 and v0.5.2, benchmark evidence was NOT carried forward: search, injection and identity paths changed, so the benchmark was re-measured on this SHA. The gates ran on the main checkout, not a git worktree, so the lifecycle-cleanup slice exercised its real cleanup surface. The packaged artifact holds 313 files, one more than v0.5.2, and that one file is docs/verification/merge-gate-pre-0.5.2.json, the archive the previous receipt commit wrote: docs/ is inside the package.json files list, so receipt commits change packaged files by construction. Only receipt files change afterwards. No push, tag, release or installed-plugin update is performed by this receipt.

memoryTiers.decidedModel: Inside a Git checkout the directory remains the project and the branch becomes the tier: a session on the default branch, or in a non-Git directory, writes project-common memory, while any other branch or worktree writes its own branch tier keyed on (project, branch). Injection and lookup read global plus project-common plus the current branch, and two worktrees of one repository on the same branch share a tier. Movement between tiers is a one-rung ladder, workstream <-> project <-> global; a skipped rung is refused, and every move appends a Chronicle PROMOTED or DEMOTED carrying from-tier, to-tier, actor and reason.
memoryTiers.behaviourChange: This changes where new memory lands. Before 0.6.0 every extracted fact went to a per-session workstream and was never read again.
memoryTiers.schemaAdditions: Additive only, and CONTINUITY_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 7: facts.tier_reason records the branch signal that placed a fact (no-branch-signal, default-branch or branch:<name>), exchanges.git_branch carries the captured branch with an idx_git_branch index, and workstreams gain branch_hint. Workstream ids are now derived deterministically from (project, branch), or from the project alone when there is no branch signal.
memoryTiers.branchCapture: The branch and the repository default branch are resolved at session start from origin/HEAD, then packed-refs, then init.defaultBranch, and propagated to exchanges.git_branch and the workstream branch_hint.
memoryTiers.automaticReconcile: The evidence-based automatic reconcile runs in the SessionStart maintenance stage as SQL with no model call.
memoryTiers.regressions: test/scope-tier-identity.test.ts (20 cases across branch signal, deterministic workstream binding for #16, exchange branch propagation, workspace location transition for #21, the default tier rule at extraction insert for #18, the untrusted-cwd quarantine for #38, and facts migrate-tiers); test/fact-tier-ladder.test.ts (11 cases across user promotion and demotion for #19, in-session KR/EN scope directives with explicit negatives, and the evidence-based automatic ladder including demotion when cited evidence is deactivated).
memoryTiers.workspaceTransition: Covered inside scope-tier-identity: workspace_id and project_id survive a directory-to-clone transition and record exactly one event, a worktree joins as a second workspace of the same project, the same remote cloned elsewhere requires explicit approval before joining, and the row updates only when .git is removed, never demoting branch memory.
memoryTiers.quarantine: Covered inside scope-tier-identity: `/` and any empty-basename path are rejected exactly like unknown, a session with an untrusted cwd stays out of any project and reads global-only, and a legacy `/` project is quarantined on migration without deleting its facts.
memoryTiers.uiFollowUp: `memex facts tier|promote|demote` is the interface today; the Web UI buttons are deferred to 0.6.1 (#22), so no UI gate covers the ladder.
memoryTiers.liveTierPlacement: NOT_PROVEN: no real session was run against the user's data root to confirm that newly extracted facts land on the intended tier, nor was the migration of that root's pre-0.6.0 workstream facts executed.

releaseConclusion: All thirteen gates PASS on the clean v0.6.0 candidate 6ba3354b, each on its first attempt: typecheck, a build that reproduced the tracked dist/, 109 files / 1102 Vitest tests, 26 Codex slices, 124 total slices including the lifecycle-cleanup slice on the main checkout, installer, marketplace, packaged runtime (memex-0.6.0.tgz, 313 files, 9 MCP tools), offline lifecycle 9/9, the real-Chrome Memex Workspace E2E (10 check groups, 0 runtime errors), 82 Workspace unit tests and the benchmark contract. Isolated plugin validation passes all 11 substitute checks with matching 0.6.0 plugin and MCP server versions, and is PASS-WITH-NOTES only because the formal `codex plugin validate` subcommand does not exist in codex-cli 0.153.4. Because this release changes the search, injection and identity paths, the benchmark evidence carried forward through v0.5.1 and v0.5.2 was retired and the full acceptance benchmark was re-measured on this SHA: PASS, 6/6 AC_PERF groups true with no threshold tuned, the knowledge map served through `loopback HTTP /api/v2/graph` with 50 nodes and 49 edges on the native LOCAL WEBGL renderer. The release itself gives memory a branch-derived tier with a one-rung promotion ladder on an additive schema that keeps continuity version 7, and reworks capsule sizing, terminal-state repair, job recovery, operator commands and injection logging; 31 new isolated cases across the tier and ladder suites and 34 across the scheduling and observability suites cover them. The v0.5.2 receipt is archived byte-for-byte as merge-gate-pre-0.6.0.json. Whether real sessions now inject at least one fact, whether newly extracted facts land on the intended tier on the user's own root, and the migration of that root's pre-0.6.0 workstream facts are NOT_PROVEN and are verified after release; live user data, an authenticated Codex tier run, the formal plugin validator, real-world performance at production corpus sizes and model quality remain NOT_PROVEN.
